subject: POC wire-up milestones & timeline — API keys, org seed, allowlist, VPC peering
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sana Patel <sana@healthsync.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC wire-up milestones & timeline — API keys, org seed, allowlist, VPC peering

Hi Sana,

Thanks again for the time earlier — excited about the proof-of-concept with HealthSync. Per our discussion I put together a short mutual action plan (MAP) focused on the environment wire‑up so your devs can start calling the API and our infra team can validate connectivity. Attached are three artifacts: a one‑page MAP playbook, an IP allowlist template, and a compact wiring checklist.

High-level proposed sequence (target: 3-week runway):
- Week 0 (this week): org tenant seed + SSO+billing contact; confirm RT/procurement timeline.
- Week 1: issue API keys (scoped test tokens), finalize IP allowlist for outbound and inbound ranges.
- Week 2: VPC peering trial (staging) + route validations; test model inferencing against a small synthetic dataset.
- Week 3: smoke tests, latency sampling, and go/no-go for expanded test traffic.

Action items for HealthSync: please confirm the security contact (name + email), provide the public IP ranges you can use for allowlist, and share an estimated procurement completion date if there are PO steps.

I copied Kimberly to loop in CS/enablement and Karthik (cc in next message) will own the peering setup. Would you be available for a 30‑minute technical handoff on Monday (Aug 18) at 10:00 AM PT?

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0183
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP_Playbook_HealthSync_v1.pdf (1 page), ip_allowlist_template.csv (1 sheet), poc-wiring-checklist.xlsx (10 rows)

From: Sana Patel <sana@healthsync.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Aug 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC wire-up milestones & timeline — API keys, org seed, allowlist, VPC peering

Thanks Ben — this looks practical and clear. A few quick questions from our side:

1) Our security team (security@healthsync.com) will need to review SOC 2 / data handling notes before we seed any environment. Can you point me to a short security pack or SOC 2 summary?
2) For the IP allowlist: we can provide a set of NAT egress ranges, but we often need a separate inbound CIDR for peering. Do you have a preferred format for that?
3) Procurement: assuming the PO needs sign‑off, we likely have a 7–10 business day cadence once the SOW is drafted. That would push some items into late Aug/early Sep unless we do temporary test tokens.

We can do Monday 8/18 at 10:00 AM PT for the handoff — I'll invite our infra lead (Darrell Chen) and the security reviewer. Can you confirm who from your side will join technically?

— Sana
Sana Patel
Director, Integrations | HealthSync, Inc.
sana@healthsync.com | (650) 555-2110

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sana Patel <sana@healthsync.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Aug 2025 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC wire-up milestones & timeline — API keys, org seed, allowlist, VPC peering

On Fri, Aug 15, 2025 at 11:03 AM Sana Patel <sana@healthsync.com> wrote:
> Thanks Ben — this looks practical and clear. A few quick questions from our side:
>
> 1) Our security team (security@healthsync.com) will need to review SOC 2 / data handling notes before we seed any environment. Can you point me to a short security pack or SOC 2 summary?
> 2) For the IP allowlist: we can provide a set of NAT egress ranges, but we often need a separate inbound CIDR for peering. Do you have a preferred format for that?
> 3) Procurement: assuming the PO needs sign‑off, we likely have a 7–10 business day cadence once the SOW is drafted. That would push some items into late Aug/early Sep unless we do temporary test tokens.

Hi Sana — quick answers inline and next steps below.

1) Security pack: attaching our SOC 2 summary + a short runbook doc pointer (see Drive link). Karthik — can you also add a note about encryption/in-transit keys we should share in the call?
2) IP allowlist format: CSV with columns: label, cidr, purpose. I attached ip_allowlist_template.csv — for peering we typically ask for the peering subnet CIDR and any NAT egress ranges. If Darrell can paste those into the template prior to the call we can validate in the meeting.
3) Procurement workaround: we can issue scoped test tokens that expire after 30 days so you can start functional tests before the PO completes. Those tokens are rate‑limited and tagged to a trial tenant.

Meeting invite: I scheduled the 30m handoff for Mon Aug 18 10:00 AM PT — calendar invite sent separately. From our side Karthik (network/infra) and I will attend; Kimberly is copied for enablement/escalation.

Next actions (pre-call):
- HealthSync: populate ip_allowlist_template.csv (Darrell) + confirm security reviewer email.
- Redwood: share SOC 2 summary link + generate trial API key for HealthSync once security contact cleared.

Thanks — talk soon.
Ben

Attachments referenced: MAP_Playbook_HealthSync_v1.pdf, ip_allowlist_template.csv, poc-wiring-checklist.xlsx
Related link: https://drive.google.com/example/healthsync-map

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Aug 2025 14:37:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: POC wire-up milestones & timeline — API keys, org seed, allowlist, VPC peering

Ben / Karthik — thanks for moving quickly on this. A couple quick notes from my side before the call:

- Prioritize the scoped test token approach so HealthSync can run functional tests even if procurement slips. Ben, please confirm token expiry (30 days) and that logs and tracing will be retained for the trial.
- Karthik, please prepare a short checklist (5 bullets) for the call about peering pre-reqs: required CIDRs, route propagation expectations, and a rollback plan if routes collide.
- Add our security contact (mina_haddad@redwood.com) to the calendar invite so HealthSync's security reviewer can exchange notes with ours during the handoff.

I'll keep an eye on the HubSpot deal (HS-2025-RED-042) and will offer a one-time enablement credit if they can commit to the three-week runway after the trial looks good.

Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
